title: Accounting Standard 23 Accounting for Investments in Associates in Consolidated Financial Statements
outcomes: Apply the equity method including goodwill and adjustments.
State disclosures and the separate-statement treatment.

meta.exam_tip: Build a carrying-amount schedule: cost → + share of profits → − dividends → ± equity changes → − unrealised profit share.

concepts.title: Associates and significant influence
body: An associate is a business over which the investor holds significant influence, other than one that is its subsidiary or joint venture.

Significant influence is the power to take part in the financial and operating policy decisions of the investee, without control. Holding 20% or more of voting power (directly or through subsidiaries) presumes it unless clearly shown otherwise; below 20% presumes its absence unless clearly shown.

Evidence includes board representation, participation in policy-making, material transactions, interchange of managerial staff and provision of essential technical information. A majority owner elsewhere does not necessarily prevent significant influence.
concepts.analogy: An associate is a company you can steer partly but not control.
concepts.work: A 25% shareholder with two directors on a 9-member board usually has significant influence.

concepts.title: The equity method
body: In consolidated financial statements, investments in associates are accounted for by the equity method: the investment is first recorded at cost and then adjusted for the investor's share of the associate's post-acquisition profits or losses.
Distributions received from the associate reduce the carrying amount.

The carrying amount is also adjusted for the investor's share of changes in the associate's equity not passing through its profit and loss, such as revaluation of fixed assets or foreign exchange translation differences.
The investor's share of the associate's results is shown in the consolidated profit and loss.
concepts.analogy: The investment grows and shrinks with the investor's share of the associate's results.
concepts.work: A 40% stake in an associate earning ₹50 lakh raises the investment by ₹20 lakh.

concepts.title: Goodwill or capital reserve and adjustments
body: On acquisition, the difference between cost and the investor's share of the associate's equity is goodwill or capital reserve. This amount sits within the investment's carrying figure and is shown separately in the notes.

Unrealised profits and losses on transactions between the investor (or its subsidiaries) and the associate are eliminated to the extent of the investor's interest. Unrealised losses are not eliminated if the transaction shows the asset is impaired.

The associate's statements are prepared to the investor's date where practicable; otherwise the most recent statements are used with adjustments for significant events. Uniform policies are used where practicable, or the fact is disclosed.
concepts.analogy: Goodwill on an associate sits inside the investment figure.
concepts.work: If the associate sells goods to the investor with ₹1 lakh profit unsold, a 30% investor eliminates ₹30,000.

concepts.title: Losses, exclusions and impairment
body: If the investor's share of losses equals or exceeds the carrying amount, the investment is reported at nil. Further losses are provided only to the extent the investor has guaranteed or committed to obligations of the associate.
When the associate later earns profits, the investor resumes recognising its share only after its share of profits equals the unrecognised losses.

The equity method is not used where the investment is acquired and held exclusively for disposal in the near future, or the associate operates under severe long-term restrictions on transferring funds; such investments follow AS 13. The equity method stops when significant influence ends.
The carrying amount is reduced for any decline in value that is other than temporary, assessed individually.
concepts.analogy: An associate's losses can wipe out the investment, but not take it below zero unless you promised to pay.
concepts.work: An investor guaranteeing an associate's bank loan continues to provide for losses beyond nil.

concepts.title: Disclosure and separate statements
body: Disclose an appropriate listing and description of associates, including proportion of ownership interest and, if different, voting power; the reasons for not applying the equity method where relevant; goodwill or capital reserve; and the share of contingencies and capital commitments.

In the consolidated balance sheet, associate investments appear as long-term investments on their own line; the share of profits or losses, and of extraordinary or prior period items, is disclosed separately.
In the investor's separate financial statements, investments in associates are carried under AS 13, usually at cost less permanent decline.
concepts.analogy: Equity method in consolidated accounts; cost in separate accounts.
concepts.work: An investor without subsidiaries does not prepare CFS and so does not apply AS 23.

mcqs.q: Significant influence is presumed when the investor holds voting power of at least:
mcqs.explain: AS 23 presumes significant influence at 20% or more of voting power, held directly or through subsidiaries, unless it can be clearly shown otherwise. Control would need more than half. In practice: weigh other evidence too.

mcqs.q: Under the equity method, dividends received from an associate:
options: Reduce the carrying amount of the investment
Are credited to profit and loss
mcqs.explain: The investor already recognises its share of profit; a dividend merely converts part of that into cash, so it reduces the carrying amount. In practice: avoid double counting income.

mcqs.q: Goodwill on acquiring an associate is:
options: Included in the carrying amount of the investment and disclosed separately
Shown as a separate intangible asset
mcqs.explain: AS 23 includes goodwill or capital reserve in the carrying amount of the investment, with separate disclosure. In practice: track it in the working.
mcqs.topic: Goodwill or capital reserve and adjustments

mcqs.q: Investment ₹10 lakh for 25%; associate's profit ₹8 lakh; dividend ₹4 lakh. Carrying amount at year end:
mcqs.explain: Add 25% of profit (₹2 lakh) and deduct 25% of dividend (₹1 lakh): 10 + 2 − 1 = ₹11 lakh. In practice: use post-acquisition figures only.

mcqs.q: Unrealised profit on sales between an investor and its associate is eliminated:
options: To the extent of the investor's interest
mcqs.explain: AS 23 eliminates unrealised profits and losses to the extent of the investor's interest in the associate, unlike full elimination for subsidiaries. In practice: multiply by the holding percentage.
mcqs.topic: Goodwill or capital reserve and adjustments

mcqs.q: When an investor's share of losses exceeds the carrying amount and it has no obligations, the investment is:
mcqs.explain: The carrying amount stops at nil; further losses are recorded only if the investor has guaranteed or committed to obligations of the associate. In practice: keep a memo of unrecognised losses.

mcqs.q: The equity method is not applied when the investment is:
options: Acquired and held exclusively for disposal in the near future
mcqs.explain: AS 23 excludes investments held exclusively for near-term disposal, and associates under severe long-term restrictions on transfer of funds; these follow AS 13. In practice: document the intention.

mcqs.q: In the investor's separate financial statements, an investment in an associate is carried:
options: Under AS 13, usually at cost less permanent decline
mcqs.explain: AS 23 applies only to consolidated financial statements; separate statements carry the investment under AS 13. In practice: two different figures may appear.

mcqs.q: An associate revalues its land upward by ₹10 lakh; the investor holds 30%. In the investor's CFS:
options: Investment increases by ₹3 lakh with a corresponding reserve
mcqs.explain: Changes in the associate's equity not passing through its profit and loss, such as revaluation, are reflected by adjusting the carrying amount for the investor's share, with the other side in reserves. In practice: keep it out of profit.

mcqs.q: Which is evidence of significant influence?
options: Representation on the board of directors
Holding 5% of shares with no board seat
mcqs.explain: Board representation, participation in policy-making, material transactions, interchange of managers and providing essential technical information all indicate significant influence. Ordinary trade or lending does not. In practice: look at governance rights.

summary: Associate: significant influence (≥ 20% presumption), not subsidiary or JV.
Equity method in CFS: cost + share of results − dividends.
Unrealised profits eliminated to investor's share.
Stop at nil unless obligations; exclusions follow AS 13.
remember: Later profits first recover unrecognised losses.
traps: Dividends reduce the investment; they are not income in CFS.

viva.model: A business over which the investor holds significant influence, and which falls outside the subsidiary and joint venture categories.
The investment is recorded at cost and adjusted for the investor's share of post-acquisition profits or losses and other equity changes, less distributions received.

viva.q: How far are unrealised profits with an associate eliminated?
viva.model: They are eliminated only up to the investor's share (interest) in the associate.

viva.q: What happens when losses exceed the investment?
viva.model: The investment is reported at nil; further losses are recognised only for guarantees or commitments, and later profits first cover the unrecognised losses.
Only in consolidated financial statements; separate statements use AS 13.

cases.title: Deepak Ltd. and Esha Ltd.
cases.case: Deepak Ltd. (which has subsidiaries) bought 40% of Esha Ltd. for ₹50 lakh when Esha's net assets were ₹110 lakh. In the year Esha earned ₹20 lakh and sold goods to Deepak at a profit of ₹5 lakh, all unsold at year end.

mcqs.explain: Deepak's share of net assets is 40% × ₹110 lakh = ₹44 lakh; cost ₹50 lakh exceeds it by ₹6 lakh, which is goodwill included in the carrying amount. In practice: disclose it separately.
mcqs.topic: Goodwill or capital reserve and adjustments

mcqs.q: Share of Esha's profit after eliminating unrealised profit:
mcqs.explain: 40% of ₹20 lakh is ₹8 lakh; less 40% of the unrealised ₹5 lakh (₹2 lakh) gives ₹6 lakh recognised. In practice: eliminate only the investor's share.
mcqs.topic: Goodwill or capital reserve and adjustments

mcqs.q: Carrying amount of the investment at year end:
mcqs.explain: Cost ₹50 lakh plus share of profit after elimination ₹6 lakh = ₹56 lakh, with no dividends received. In practice: disclose goodwill within it.
